How to use R and RStudio (Mac)

With these steps you can use R and RStudio in the browser you usually use (Chrome, Safari and so on). You do not need to install R or RStudio on your computer. The only app to install is Docker Desktop. Every computer analyses with the same versions of R and the packages.

Steps
  1. Install Docker Desktop (once, first)
  2. Extract the Zip and place the folder
  3. Start (RStudio opens)
  4. Analyse in RStudio
  5. Stop
  6. If something goes wrong

1Install Docker Desktop (once, first)

Docker Desktop is the app that runs R and RStudio. Install it by following Docker's official guide (Docker Desktop for Mac), and start it once (no account is needed). Choose "Apple silicon" for an Apple silicon Mac (M1 or later) and "Intel chip" for an Intel Mac.

Notes It is safest to have at least 10 GB of free disk space (the environment itself uses about 4 GB).
Docker Desktop is free for personal use, education, non-commercial open source and small businesses (fewer than 250 employees and less than 10 million US dollars in annual revenue). Work in larger organizations and use in government entities need a paid subscription. Check your organization's rules (Docker's explanation).

2Extract the Zip and place the folder

Double-click the Zip you received; a folder is created in the same place. Put that folder wherever you like.

The folder contains several files. These are the ones you use.

FileWhen to use it
HOW_TO_USE_Mac.htmlThis guide.
start_mac.commandUse it to start the first time (step 3).
Start RStudio (Start RStudio.app)The launcher window app. From the second time on, double-click it to start.
diagnose_mac.commandDiagnoses the environment when it does not start well (If something goes wrong).
notebooks/README.mdHow to write analyses (step 4).
TEMPLATE_VERSION.txtWhich version of the environment this is. Send its contents when you ask for help.
Places to avoid Avoid folders synced by iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and the like (reading and writing become slow, and files can conflict). On a Mac, Desktop and Documents may be synced by iCloud Drive (when the Finder sidebar lists "Desktop" and "Documents" under "iCloud"). In that case, use a place that is not synced (for example, the Downloads folder).

To keep each analysis in its own folder, copy the whole extracted folder (the Docker names are made from the folder's name and location, so the copies do not conflict).

3Start

The first time

Because the files came from the internet, macOS blocks start_mac.command with a message that it "could not be opened" if you just double-click it. The first time, start it with A or B.

A. Start from Terminal
  1. In the Finder menu choose "Go" → "Utilities", and double-click "Terminal" (or press command+space, type "Terminal" and open it).
  2. In the Terminal window, type bash followed by one space, drag start_mac.command from the Finder into the Terminal window, and press Enter.
  3. When the "R analysis environment (RStudio)" window appears, you may close Terminal.
B. Press "Open Anyway" in System Settings (needs your Mac password or Touch ID)
  1. Double-click start_mac.command; when it says it could not be opened, close the message with "Done".
  2. Open the Apple menu → "System Settings" → "Privacy & Security", and scroll down to "Security".
  3. Press "Open Anyway" and enter your password or Touch ID. If a confirmation appears, press "Open Anyway" again (if it does not, double-click start_mac.command again).

Always start the first time from start_mac.command (it removes the "downloaded from the internet" mark from the files in this folder and opens the launcher window app).

What happens when it starts

  1. If you are asked whether to allow access to a folder, check that it is the folder you are using, and allow it.
  2. The "R analysis environment (RStudio)" window appears and preparation begins. The first time takes from a few minutes to over ten minutes (an internet connection is needed). After that it takes tens of seconds.
  3. When it is ready, "RStudio is ready" appears and RStudio opens in your browser automatically.
ButtonWhen to use it
StartTo start again after stopping with "Stop".
Open in browserWhen RStudio does not open, or you closed the browser tab.
Copy addressWhen "Open in browser" does not work either; paste it into the browser's address bar (it starts with http://localhost:).
StopWhen you are finished (step 5).
  • The box at the bottom of the window shows the progress (text scrolling by is normal; if it seems to stop, keep waiting).
  • If Docker Desktop was not running, "Starting Docker Desktop..." appears first, and it waits for Docker Desktop to start.
  • The port number in the address may change each time you start.

Keep the "R analysis environment (RStudio)" window open until you finish your analysis.

Starting from the second time

If the "R analysis environment (RStudio)" window is still open, press "Start" in it. If you closed the window, double-click "Start RStudio" in this folder in the Finder (A and B are not needed).

4Analyse in RStudio

In RStudio, this folder appears as /app. Your files are saved in this folder, so they are kept when you stop.

  • How to write analyses (where notebooks go and how results are recorded) is in notebooks/README.md in this folder.
  • Put data under data/ (see data/README.md).
  • The steps in README.md and docs/ that use git or make (git clone, make rename, make hooks and so on) are not needed when you received a Zip. Steps 3 and 5 of this guide are all you need to start and stop.
  • Type the make commands in notebooks/README.md (such as make render) in the "Terminal" tab of RStudio (they do not work in the Mac Terminal app).

Adding packages

If you use install.packages() in RStudio, the package is installed only for that session and is gone when you stop. Instead, add the package names to the end of DESCRIPTION in this folder as below, and start again (the package list is rebuilt, which takes from a few minutes to over ten minutes).

Config/Needs/project:
    tidyverse,
    here
  • You can add packages that are on CRAN. Separate the names with commas.
  • Write the "Config/Needs/project:" line only once; from the second time on, add names below it.
  • A package that fails to load may need a system library. In that case, add the names of the apt packages it needs to docker/project_apt.txt, one per line, and start again.
  • If RStudio does not open because a name is wrong, in Finder, right-click DESCRIPTION → "Open With" → "TextEdit", fix it, save it, and press "Start" again.

5Stop

  1. Save any unsaved work in RStudio.
  2. Press "Stop" in the "R analysis environment (RStudio)" window.
  3. When it says "Stopped", you may close the "R analysis environment (RStudio)" window and the browser tab (if you keep the window open, "Start" starts it again).
  • If you try to close the window before stopping, "Stop and quit?" appears. "Stop and quit" stops the environment and then closes the window ("Back" returns to your work).
  • The built image is kept, so the next start is faster. When you start again, you can carry on where you left off.
  • You may leave Docker Desktop running or quit it (to quit: the whale icon in the menu bar → "Quit Docker Desktop").

?If something goes wrong

If the top of the window says "Starting or stopping failed", look up the last line of the box at the bottom of the window in this table.

MessageWhat to do
Put this file inside the analysis folder, the folder that contains docker-compose.yml, and use it from thereCheck that you have not deleted files in the folder or moved them elsewhere. If you are not sure, extract the Zip you received again (step 2).
Docker Desktop was not foundInstall Docker Desktop as in step 1.
Docker Desktop did not become readyOpen the Docker Desktop window, wait until "Engine running" appears at the bottom left, and press "Start" again.
Could not create the file for checking DockerCheck that there is free disk space, restart the Mac, and press "Start" again.
Could not prepare the environmentCheck that you are connected to the internet and have free disk space, and press "Start" again.
Could not rebuild the package listFirst check that you are connected to the internet. If you added packages to DESCRIPTION, check their names (a name on CRAN, the spelling, the commas between names), fix them, and press "Start" again (step 4). RStudio does not open in this case, so in Finder, right-click DESCRIPTION → "Open With" → "TextEdit" and fix it there.
Could not start RStudioCheck that Docker Desktop is running, and press "Start" again. If it keeps happening, diagnose the environment and send the result when you ask for help.
RStudio does not respondPress "Start" again. If it keeps happening, diagnose the environment and send the result when you ask for help.
Could not stopCheck that Docker Desktop is running, and press "Stop" again.

Diagnose the environment

In a Terminal window, type bash and one space, drag in diagnose_mac.command, and press Enter (the same as A in step 3). It checks your computer, this folder and Docker without starting or changing anything.

  • The first line gives the result (prerequisites met / preparation needed / some items unverified), and the [fail], [warning] and [unknown] lines show each item and why. The results of the last three starts are shown too.
  • The result is kept in outputs/launcher/environment_check_<date and time>_<ID>.json (your user name and folder location are replaced with <LOCAL_PATH>).

Options (type them after diagnose_mac.command with a space before pressing Enter):

OptionWhat it does
--networkChecks that the image and package sources can be reached over the internet (nothing is downloaded).
--share-testChecks with the built image that files can be read and written between this folder and the container.
--incident=launch_<launch ID>.jsonlSummarizes one failed start and keeps it in outputs/launcher/incident_<launch ID>.json.

When you ask for help

  • Copy the messages shown in the box at the bottom of the launcher window exactly (you can select and copy the text in the box).
  • Also send the contents of TEMPLATE_VERSION.txt (which version of the environment it is).
  • The progress of each start is kept in outputs/launcher/launch_<launch ID>.jsonl (only stage names, times and exit codes; no data or analysis contents). Attach it with the diagnosis result.
